skeleton.description: Concatenate two text files into one output file with newline-boundary normalisation.

state.name: validate
state.contract:
Read config.file1, config.file2, config.output, and config.encoding.
Perform all checks before taking any action: 1. Verify config.file1 exists and is readable (fs.accessSync with R_OK). If it fails, emit a clear error message that names config.file1 and return INVALID. 2. Verify config.file2 exists and is readable in the same way. If it fails, emit a clear error message that names config.file2 and return INVALID. 3. Resolve the absolute paths of config.file1, config.file2, and config.output using path.resolve. If the resolved config.output equals the resolved config.file1 or config.file2, emit an error describing the collision ("output path collides with input path: <path>") and return INVALID.
If all three checks pass, return VALID. Write nothing to the output directory.

state.name: concat
state.contract:
Read config.file1, config.file2, config.output, and config.encoding.
Steps: 1. Read the full textual content of config.file1 as a string using config.encoding. 2. Read the full textual content of config.file2 as a string using config.encoding. 3. Newline normalisation: if content1 is non-empty and does NOT end with '
', append exactly one '
' to content1. If content1 is empty or already ends with '
', leave it unchanged (do NOT insert an extra blank line). 4. Form the combined string: combined = content1 + content2. 5. Atomic write: a. Determine a temporary file path in the same directory as config.output (e.g. config.output + '.tmp.' + process.pid) to keep the rename on one filesystem. b. Write combined to the temporary path using config.encoding. c. Rename (fs.renameSync) the temporary path to the final config.output path. This guarantees the output is either complete or absent — never partially written. 6. Compute the byte length of the written content (Buffer.byteLength(combined, config.encoding)). 7. Set c.data.outputBytes to that byte count. 8. Emit a success message: "Written <config.output> (<byteCount> bytes)".
Return DONE on success. On any I/O error at any step (read, write, or rename), emit a human-readable error message describing what failed and which path was involved, then return ERROR.
